title: verifierVerificationLevel is still seeded, stored, served and admin-editable but enforced nowhere after KS-1628
description:
**After KS-1628, a document type's** `verifierVerificationLevel` **is still seeded, stored, served and admin-editable, but enforced nowhere.** Wednesday ruled (a) on KS-1628 PR 2: retire the gate with the route, and file this ticket. **The options below are for the owner to choose between; this ticket does not choose.**

## What happened

The only place the per-type verifier level was enforced was api-gateway's own handler for `POST /api/documents/:id/verify` (`routes/verification.ts`, the level check at develop `:596-608`): it read the document type's `verifierVerificationLevel` and refused a caller below it with 403 `INSUFFICIENT_VERIFICATION_LEVEL` (pinned by `ks1176` section E). KS-1628 retires that route.

**Still present, measured at develop** `83ed01af70fd`**:**

* seeded: `api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts`, nine document types each carry a `verifierVerificationLevel`;
* stored and edited: originate `routes/adminConfig.ts:202`, `:234`, `:1768`;
* served: api-gateway `routes/platform.ts:895` and the document-types route (`routes/verification.ts`).

**Enforced:** nowhere. `meetsVerificationLevel` survives in `services/enforcement.ts:153`, but that is the CREATOR level on document create. The successor `POST /api/verification/verify` is public by design (KS-442).

**Real effect today:** none — the one enforcement point had 0 calls at the edge on kintsugi (\~30 days) and demo (\~38 days), measured read-only 2026-10-19. The risk is a **misleading control**: an administrator who sets a verifier level will reasonably believe it restricts who can verify a document of that type.

## Options for the owner

1. **Remove the setting** — drop `verifierVerificationLevel` from the type catalogue, the admin UI and the stores.
2. **Label it inert** in the admin UI ("not enforced since KS-1628") and leave the data.
3. **Re-introduce a verifier-level gate on a non-public verify route** (the public successor is public by design, so a gate there would contradict KS-442).

## Related

* **KS-1190** ("meetsVerificationLevel fails open on an unknown REQUIRED level") has two halves. Its **verify** half cites `routes/verification.ts:554-557`, which KS-1628 removes, so that half no longer applies; its **create** half (`POST /api/documents`) is unaffected.
* `VerificationRouteDeps.meetsVerificationLevel` is now unused by the routes and kept only so existing test doubles still type-check (comment in place; removable together with whichever option is chosen).

## Dedupe

`description: contains` over all issues: `verifierVerificationLevel` 1 (KS-1190), `verifier_verification_level` 1 (KS-1190), `meetsVerificationLevel` 3 (KS-1628, KS-1190, KS-1176), `verifier level` 0. None records the setting as inert. Control: a nonsense literal returns 0.

Filed by Seat R 49th from KS-1628 PR 2. Not built.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Kam ruled the 31-decision card `secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109` on 2026-11-09 at 13:44:07 (live board), in these words: "Decision secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109: a — All recommendations (A and B)". Option a reads: "Every row ruled as recommended; a board seat files and moves the tickets; the KS-607 demo rows still wait for a separate yes." This ticket is row A10 of the decision pack, ruled as recommended: option 1. Remove the admin setting "verifier verification level": public verify is public by ruling (KS-442), so the gate cannot come back on that route, and the setting misleads admins.

A build seat does the work; nothing was changed in code by this comment.

Alongside this comment the ticket, which was unassigned, is assigned to the board account, and moves from Backlog to Todo.
